subject: Post-incident evidence briefing and checklist for Skyline Payments
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@skylinepayments.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Incident questions — immediate evidence request

Marissa —

Thanks for the heads up about last night's service interruption. Our security team is asking for a short written confirmation that Skyline customer data was not exfiltrated and a brief summary of the forensic evidence you have so far. Specifically:

- Any confirmed external S3 reads during the window (source IPs / principals)
- Whether any tokens/credentials were accessed or rotated
- Snapshot of relevant audit logs (S3, auth, firewall) or a pointer where we can pull them

We appreciate a short note we can attach to our internal postmortem. If you can include an expected ETA for a fuller evidence bundle, that would be helpful.

Elena
Elena Torres
Head of IT Security, Skyline Payments
elena.torres@skylinepayments.com
(555) 312-9941

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@skylinepayments.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 10:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Incident questions — immediate evidence request

Hi Elena —

Thanks for flagging this. We're assembling a concise evidence package and can confirm we are prioritizing the items you listed. Initial updates:

- Containment: the transient ingestion path implicated in the incident was isolated at 02:18 UTC and the suspicious process was terminated.
- Access controls: we rotated the short-lived service tokens for the affected worker pool and revoked the associated session credentials at 03:05 UTC.
- Preliminary log review: no anomalous long-running S3 GET operations from external IPs were observed in the first sweep.

I'm copying Sean (security lead), Laura (ops), and Priya (customer security liaison) to pull the artifact set and confirm. We expect a short summary for you within 48 hours and a full artifact bundle (logs + manifest + checksums) within 72 hours.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success (Security Escalations)
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: incident-briefing-stub.txt (plain text, 2 KB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Incident questions — immediate evidence request

Team —

Elena from Skyline is requesting an evidence bundle to confirm whether any customer data was exfiltrated during Friday's disruption. Please treat as high priority. Requested artifacts/ask from customer: S3 access snapshot, auth token rotation timeline, consolidated SIEM alerts, and a short summary paragraph we can send to them.

Priority checklist:
- [ ] Pull S3 access logs for bucket prefix skyl-payments/* between 01:45–03:30 UTC
- [ ] Export relevant CloudTrail events and correlate with rotated tokens
- [ ] Generate manifest with file hashes + README explaining collection process
- [ ] Quick claim: one-paragraph statement on whether any indicators of exfiltration were observed (if none, say so explicitly)

Laura — can you take the log pulls and generate the CSV snapshot? Sean — can you run the IOC sweep across the SIEM and confirm no suspicious outbound transfers? Priya — once we have artifacts, please sanitize and package for Skyline.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Incident questions — immediate evidence request

Folks — quick findings from the sweep (high-level):

- S3 access snapshot (attached): we found no external-origin GET/PUT operations for the Skyline prefixes during the window. All S3 requests were from internal worker principals or our backup service account. (Attachment: s3-access-snapshot-20270515.csv)
- CloudTrail/STS: token rotations occurred as Marissa noted. No role assumption events from unknown principals after containment.
- Egress/Network: firewall proxies show normal outbound patterns; we did not observe large aggregated uploads to third-party hosts.
- SIEM IOCs: ran YARA + custom patterns on the relevant agent telemetry — no matches consistent with data exfiltration.
- Integrity checks: generated manifest with SHA256 hashes for ingested files in the window and reconciled against our storage index. No missing objects found. (Attachment: checksum-manifest-20270515.txt)

Caveat: while our internal evidence does not indicate exfiltration, we cannot assert with 100% mathematical certainty absence of all exposures (there are always blind spots). That said, given the telemetry breadth (S3, CloudTrail, egress proxies, agent telemetry), the evidence set is strong and we are comfortable stating 'no indicators of customer data exfiltration observed within the review window'.

I'll assemble a concise evidence summary PDF and package the attachments for Priya to sanitize before customer delivery.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Security Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: forensic-summary-20270515.pdf (PDF, 1.2 MB)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@skylinepayments.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:44:00 -07:00
Subject: Final evidence briefing — Skyline Payments (post-incident)

Hi Elena —

Attached is the evidence bundle from our post-incident investigation. Summary (short):

- Scope: reviewed collections across S3 access logs, CloudTrail, egress proxy logs, agent telemetry, and our SIEM for the period 2027-05-14 01:30:00 UTC through 2027-05-15 04:00:00 UTC.
- Findings: no indicators of customer data exfiltration were observed in the reviewed telemetry. We observed expected internal access patterns and confirmed rotation of affected short-lived tokens after containment.
- Artifacts attached: forensic-summary-20270515.pdf (executive summary), s3-access-snapshot-20270515.csv (filtered S3 access for skyline-payments/*), checksum-manifest-20270515.txt (SHA256 hashes + collection README).
- Controls taken: immediate containment at 02:18 UTC, token rotation at 03:05 UTC, and accelerated retention of relevant logs for 90 days for any follow-up audit.

Action items for Skyline if you'd like them:
- We can provide a signed checksum manifest and an HMAC of the PDF bundle for your chain-of-custody records.
- If your security team wants a live walkthrough with Sean and Laura, we can schedule a 45-minute call and share the raw logs under the NDA you proposed.

Plain statement you may use in your postmortem: 
"Redwood conducted a forensic review of the affected services and, based on S3, CloudTrail, egress, and agent telemetry for the incident window, observed no indicators of customer data exfiltration."

If you'd like us to soften or expand the wording for your internal audience, tell us and we'll iterate. Thanks again for your patience — we'll remain on-call for any follow-ups.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success (Security Escalations)
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: forensic-summary-20270515.pdf, s3-access-snapshot-20270515.csv, checksum-manifest-20270515.txt]
